content:
HubSpot Company Record — Lattice Health Systems

Summary
- Healthcare SaaS (patient engagement + clinician workflows). Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for regulated workloads.
- Current pain: internal teams report "silent" model changes from other vendors. Procurement/security pushing for change visibility + rollback documentation as a gating requirement.
- Focused on predictable throughput/latency and stable outputs across releases.

Firmographics
- HQ: US (NA). Primary customers: US provider networks.
- Regulated environment (HIPAA). Asks about BAA readiness and data handling in Dedicated.

Products / Scope
- Primary: Dedicated (GPU pool with isolation).
- Secondary: Optimize (cost/perf tooling) if it helps control spend and prevent regressions.

Use cases (as described by customer)
- Clinician note summarization (structured output requirements; strict formatting).
- Patient portal assistant (chat; high sensitivity to tone/safety; needs guardrails).
- Internal doc search (embeddings + reranking) across policies and clinical guidance.

Key Requirements (Evaluation)
1) Customer-facing model change history + release notes
- Wants a per-model/per-version history that can be referenced during incidents: exact version promoted, when, and which deployment was affected.
- Release notes must answer: what changed, why it changed, how risky, and how to roll back.
- Explicitly asked for consistent taxonomy (breaking/perf/quality/bugfix/deprecation/security) and a clear "public vs internal" separation.

2) Rollout policies for Dedicated
- Needs control over rollout eligibility (no auto-promote without approval in certain environments).
- Wants canary + A/B options and the ability to pin versions by environment (staging vs prod) and by route.
- Asked whether rollback is instantaneous (routing) vs requires redeploy.

3) Rollback guidance + operational runbooks
- Procurement wants written rollback steps for Dedicated: revert to previous model version, expected time-to-stability, and any compatibility constraints.
- Asked for "what happens if tokenizer/runtime requirements change" and how Redwood prevents breaking pinned versions.

4) Security/compliance
- Audit logging: who changed what metadata/version, when, and which deployment (Dedicated/VPC). Needs export to SIEM.
- Retention controls: expects ability to retain audit logs and change history for >= 12 months.
- KMS: preference for customer-managed keys where applicable; at minimum documented encryption-at-rest model.
- Data residency: US-only hosting for Dedicated deployment.

Performance / SLO notes (early)
- Latency target: P95 < 1.5s for typical chat responses (short outputs); tolerant of longer for summaries but wants consistency.
- Throughput: expects predictable concurrency for weekday peaks; prefers reserved capacity over burst unpredictability.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-09-18: Company record created after inbound request: "Dedicated + rollout controls".
- 2025-09-24: Discovery call (Liam O'Rourke + Felix Schneider). Key ask: model version pinning + no silent updates.
- 2025-10-02: Shared security FAQ + early Dedicated sizing estimate (Drive stubs).
- 2025-10-08: Technical deep dive (Fireflies: 2025-10-08-lattice-dedicated-technical-deep-dive-rollouts-and-release-notes). Walked through rollouts, A/B, pinning, fallback concepts. Customer requested screenshots/mock of change history + example release notes.
- 2025-10-11: Internal sync w/ Console & Tooling team on timelines for release notes + change history surfaces; flagged as procurement blocker.
- 2025-10-14: Customer follow-up email: "Need formal rollback doc + release note sample to move to procurement".

Notable quotes / call notes
- "We can’t take model updates on faith. If outputs drift, we need to show an auditor what changed and when."
- "Our SRE team wants a simple answer: which version is serving right now, and how do we roll back?"
- "If there’s a breaking change, we need it called out clearly, not buried in a generic changelog."

Risks / Watchouts
- Needs careful alignment on what is customer-visible vs internal-only (they want transparency but Redwood must avoid leaking sensitive operational details).
- They may choose AWS Bedrock/Azure OpenAI for procurement simplicity unless we provide strong change visibility artifacts.

Next steps (internal)
- Provide: (1) sample customer-facing release note artifact for a model promotion, (2) explanation of rollback + version pinning in Dedicated, (3) audit log event overview (public description), (4) Console mock / short walkthrough of model change history.
- Align with Product (Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes) on how we position upcoming unified metadata + changelog generator (timeline + what’s GA vs beta).

Internal links / references
- Fireflies transcript: 2025-10-08-lattice-dedicated-technical-deep-dive-rollouts-and-release-notes
- Drive: gdrive://shared_drives/customer-success/customer-facing-change-visibility-faq-draft.json
- Notes: Customer cited recent incident at another vendor where model behavior changed without notification; this is driving strict approval gates + audit needs.
